questions.q: Consider the circle $x^2+y^2-4 x-2 y+c=0$ whose centre is $A(2,1)$. If the point $P(10,7)$ is such that the line segment $P A$ meets the circle in $Q$ with $P Q=5$, then $c$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given equation of circle is $x^2+y^2-4 x-2 y+c=0$ whose centre is $A(2,1)$.
Now, $A P=\sqrt{(2-10)^2+(1-7)^2}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{(-8)^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{64+36}=\sqrt{100} \\ & =10\end{aligned}\therefore \quad A Q=A P-P Q=10-5=5$ So, $Q$ is the mid-point of AP $=\left(\frac{10+2}{2}, \frac{7+1}{2}\right)=(6,4)$ Since, $Q$ lies on a circle. $\begin{array}{rlrl}& \therefore & 6^2+4^2-4(6)-2(4)+c & =0 \\ & \Rightarrow & 36+16-24-8+c & =0 \\ & \Rightarrow & 20+c & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & c & =-20\end{array}$

questions.q: The intercept on the line y = x by the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x = 0$ is $AB$ . The equation of the circle with $AB$ as a diameter is ……
questions.solution:
We have equation of line y = x and equation of circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x = 0$

Now, intersecting points of given line and circle
$x^{2} + x^{2} - 2x = 0$
$⇒ 2x^{2} - 2x = 0$
$⇒ 2x\left(x - 1\right) = 0$
$⇒ x = 0,1$
When x = 0 then y =0 when x =1 then y = 1
$∴$ Coordinates of end points of diameter AB are (0, 0) and (1, 1)
$∴$ Required equation of circle with diameter AB
\left(x - 0\right)\left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 0\right)\left(y - 1\right) = 0$
$⇒ x^{2} - 2 + y^{2} - y = 0$
$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - x - y = 0

questions.q: The abscissa of $A$ and $B$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2} + 2ax - b^{2} = 0$ and their ordinates are the roots of the equation $y^{2} + 2py - q^{2} = 0$. The equation of the circle with $AB$ as diameter is
questions.solution:
Let, $A ≡ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)andB ≡ \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)

${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}$ are roots of $x^{2} + 2ax - b^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left($x - {x}_{1}\$right)\left($x - {x}_{2}\right) = x^{2} + 2ax - b^{2}$

${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}$ are roots of $y^{2} + 2py - q^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left($y - {y}_{1}\right)\left(y - {y}_{2}\right) = y^{2} + 2py - q^{2}$

Now, equation of circle with $AB$ as diameter is

\left(x - {x}_{1}\right)\left(x - {x}_{2}\right) + \left(y - {y}_{1}\$right)\left($y - {y}_{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + 2ax - b^{2} + y^{2} + 2py - q^{2} = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + 2ax + 2py - b^{2} - q^{2} = 0$

questions.q: The locus of the centre of a circle which cuts the circle $x^{2} - 20x + y^{2} + 4 = 0$ orthogonally and also touches the line $x = 2$ is
questions.solution:
Let the general equation of circle be

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ ....... (i)

It cuts the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 20x + 4 = 0$ orthogonally

$∴ 2\left(- 10g + 0 \times f\right) = c + 4 ⇒ - 20g = c + 4$ .......(ii)

$∵$ circle (i) touches $x = 2$

therefore, perpendicular distance from centre to the tangent to the circle=radius

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{- g + 0 - 2}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {0}^{2}}}\right| = \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}$

$⇒ {\left(g + 2\right)}^{2} = g^{2} + f^{2} - c$

$⇒ g^{2} + 4 + 4g = g^{2} + f^{2} - c ⇒ 4g + 4 = f^{2} - c$ ... (iii)

on eliminating $c$ from (ii) and (iii) we get

$- 16g + 4 = f^{2} + 4 ⇒ f^{2} + 16g = 0$

Hence, locus of \left(- g, - f\right)$ is,

$y^{2} - 16x = 0$ (replacing $- f$ & $- g$ by $x$ & $y$ )$

$\begin{aligned} & S=x^2+y^2+4 x+6 y-3=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(x+2)^2+(y+2)^2=4^2\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{OP}^2=\mathrm{AP}^2+\mathrm{OA}^2 \Rightarrow 5^2=4^2+\mathrm{AP}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{AP}=3 \\ & \text { Let } \angle \mathrm{AOP}=\angle \mathrm{BOP}=\theta \\ & \sin \theta=\frac{3}{5} \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{4}{5} \\ & \sin 2 \theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta=2 \times \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{4}{5}=\frac{24}{25} \\ & \Delta \mathrm{AOB}=\frac{1}{2} \times \mathrm{OA} \times \mathrm{OB} \sin 2 \theta \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4 \times \frac{24}{25}=\frac{192}{25} \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{OAP}=\Delta \mathrm{AOP}-\Delta \mathrm{AOQ} \\ & =\Delta \mathrm{AOP}-\frac{\Delta \mathrm{AOB}}{2} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3-\frac{96}{25}=6-\frac{96}{25}=\frac{54}{25} \\ & \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{PAB}=2 \times \Delta \mathrm{OAP}=2 \times \frac{54}{25}=\frac{108}{25}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The equation of the circle whose diameter is common chord to the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}+2 a x+c=0$ and $x^{2}+y^{2}+2 b y+c=0$ is
questions.solution: Let $S_{1} \equiv x^{2}+y^{2}+2 a x+c=0$ and $S_{2} \equiv x^{2}+y^{2}+2 b y+c=0$ Equation of common chord as a diameter of the third circle $\begin{aligned}$S_{1}-S_{2} &=0 \\ a x-b y &=0 \\ y &=$\frac{a x}{b}...($i) \end{aligned} On putting the value of $y$ in Eq. (i), we get $\begin{array}{r}$x^{2}+\left(\frac{a^{2} x^{2}}{b^{2}}\right)+$2 a x+c=0 \\ \left($a^{2}+b^{2}\right) x^{2}+2 a b^{2} x+c b^{2}=0 \end{array} Let $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ be the roots of the equation. $\therefore \quad x_{1}+x_{2}=\frac{-2 a b^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and $x_{1} x_{2}=\frac{c b^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ Similarly, \left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right) y^{2}+2 b a^{2} y+c a^{2}=0$ Let $y_{1}$ and $y_{2}$ be the roots of the equation $\therefore \quad y_{1}+y_{2}=\frac{-2 a^{2} b}{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and $\quad y_{1} y_{2}=\frac{c a^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ Now, the required equation of third circle \left(x-x_{1}\right)\left(x-x_{2}\right)+\left(y-y_{1}\right)\left(y-y_{2}\right)=0x^{2}-\left(x_{1}+x_{2}\right) x+x_{1} x_{2}+y^{2}-\left(y_{1}+y_{2}\right) y+y_{1} y_{2}=0x^{2}+y^{2}+\frac{2 a b^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}} \cdot x+\frac{2 b a^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}} \cdot y+\frac{c b^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}}+\frac{c a^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}}=0\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+\frac{2 a b^{2}}{a^{2}+b^{2}} \cdot x+\frac{2 a^{2} b}{a^{2}+b^{2}} \cdot y+\frac{c\left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right)}{\left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right)}=0\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+\frac{2 a b^{2}}{\left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right)} \cdot x+\frac{2 a^{2} b}{\left(a^{2}+b^{2}\right)} \cdot y+c=0$

questions.q: $P$ is a point  \left(a, b\right)$ in the first quadrant. If the two circles which pass through $P$ and touch both the coordinate axes, cut at right angles, then :$
questions.solution:
Let the equation of circle& which touches both coordinate axes is&

\left(x - r\right)2 + \left(y - r\right)2 = r^{2}$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - 2rx - 2ry + r^{2} = 0$

where,~$r$~is radius.

It is passing through~ \left(a, b\right)$, so

$r^{2} - 2 ( a + b ) r + \left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right) = 0$

Let the roots of this equation are~${r}_{1}, {r}_{2}$

Sum of roots

${r}_{1} + {r}_{2} = 2 \left(a + b\right)$

Product of roots

${r}_{1} \cdot {r}_{2} =a^{2} + b^{2}$

Both circles intersect orthogonally each other so

$2{r}_{1}{r}_{2} + 2{r}_{1}{r}_{2} = {r}_{1}^{2} + {r}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ 6{r}_{1}{r}_{2} = \left({r}_{1} + {r}_{2}\right)2$

$⇒ 6\left(a^{2} + b^{2}\right) = 4 ( a + b{)}^{2}$

$⇒ a^{2} - 4ab + b^{2} = 0$

questions.q: If the circle& $x^{2} + y^{2} + 2{a}_{1}x + c = 0$~lies completely inside the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} + 2{a}_{2}x + c = 0,$& then
questions.solution:
We have,

The circle& $x^{2} + y^{2} + 2{a}_{1}x + c = 0$, with centre~${C}_{1} \left(- {a}_{1},0\right)$

and circle~$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2{a}_{2}x + c = 0$, with centre~${C}_{2} \left(- {a}_{2},0\right)$

Equation of radical axis of the given circles is $x = 0$.~If one circle lies completely inside the other, then the centre of both circles should lie on the same side of radical axis and radical axis should not intersect the circles.

$⇒ {a}_{1}{a}_{2} > 0$

Putting~$x = 0$~(equation of radical axis)~to anyone of the circle, we get,

~$y^{2} + c = 0$.

For imaginary roots,~$c > 0$& (radical axis should not intersect the circles).

questions.q: The equation of the circle circumscribing the triangle formed by the lines $x + y = 6, 2x + y = 4$~and~$x + 2y = 5$ is
questions.solution:
Let the triangle thus formed is $△ ABC$, where

$AB: x + y = 6, BC: 2x + y = 4$~

and~$CA: x + 2y = 5$

Now we can find coordinates of point $A, B$~and~$C$~by solving these three eqautions.
Solving $AB$ and $BC$,
we get $B \left(-2, 8\right)$.
Similarly we get,~

$A \left(7, - 1\right)$~and $C \left(1, 2\right)$.

Now let the equation of circle passing through vertices of~$△ ABC$~is~$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$

Now, point~$A, BandC$~will satisfy this general equation.~

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$

$⇒ \left(7\right)2 + \left(-1\right)2 + 2g\left(7\right) + 2f\left(-1\right) + c = 0 \ldots \left\{A\right\}$

$⇒ \left(-2\right)2 + \left(8\right)2 + 2g\left(-2\right) + 2f\left(8\right) + c = 0 ⋯ \left\{B\right\}$

$⇒ \left(1\right)2 + \left(2\right)2 + 2g\left(1\right) + 2f\left(2\right) + c = 0 \ldots \left\{C\right\}$

Solving these three equations for~$g, f$~and~$c$~we get,

$⇒ 50 + 14g - 2f + c = 0 \ldots \left\{A\right\}$

$⇒ 68 - 4g + 16f + c = 0 \ldots \left\{B\right\}$

$⇒ 5 + 2g + 4f + c = 0 \ldots \left\{C\right\}$

$⇒ 18 - 18g + 18f = 0 = 2 - 2g + 2f = 0$

$⇒ 63 - 6g + 12f = 0 = 21 - 2g + 4f = 0$

$⇒ f = $\dfrac{- 19}{2}

$⇒ g = $\dfrac{- 17}{2}

$⇒ c = 50$

Hence equation will be,

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 17x - 19y + 50 = 0$

Hence, Option $4& is the answer.

$

questions.q: If $P$ is a point such that the ratio of the square of the lengths of the tangents from $P$ to the circles $x^2+y^2+2 x-4 y-20=0$ and $x^2+y^2-4 x+2 y-2 y-44=0$ is $2: 3$, then the locus of $P$ is a circle with centre :

Let co-ordinates of $P$ be  \left(x_1, y_1\right)$.
Given that,
$x^2+y^2+2 x-4 y-20=0$ ...(i)
and $\quad x^2+y^2-4 x+2 y-44=0$ ...(ii)
Length of the tangent from $P$ to Eq. (i)
$=x_1^2+y_1^2+2 x_1-4 y_1-20$ ...(iii)
Length of the tangent from $P$ to Eq. (ii)
$=x_1^2+y_1^2-4 x_1+2 y_1-44$ ...(iv)
Given that ratio of lengths of tangent $=\frac{2}{3}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x_1^2+y_1^2+2 x_1-4 y_1-20}{x_1^2+y_1^2-4 x_1+2 y_1-44}=\frac{2}{3}\Rightarrow \quad 3 x_1^2+3 y_1^2+6 x_1-12 y_1-60=2 x_1^2+2 y_1^2-8 x_1+4 y_1-88\Rightarrow \quad x_1^2+y_1^2+14 x_1-16 y_1+28=0\therefore$ Locus of points $P$ is
$x^2+y^2+14 x-16 y+28=0$
Centre of the circle is $(-7,8)$.$
